clinicalDetails.clinicalHistory: The patient was apparently normal eight months ago when she was involved in a road traffic accident resulting in a left tibial condal fracture and an evulsion ACL tear. Open reduction and internal fixation was performed by Dr. Hemant Galyan, followed by four to six weeks of non-weight bearing and subsequent progressive loading. Despite eight months having passed, the patient has not returned to full functional activity and presented for further management.
clinicalDetails.chiefComplaint: Left knee pain, difficulty walking and performing functional activities

subjectiveAssessments.conclusion: Moderate pain with mild irritability particularly during prolonged walking and standing; relieved with rest.
Difficulty walking, prolonged standing, and performing daily functional activities.

tests.comments: Restricted and painful knee flexion on overpressure
Restricted knee extension (left 20 deg vs right extension)
Restricted ankle dorsiflexion on affected left side
Healed surgical scar on medial aspect of left knee with swelling noted

subjectiveGoals.goalDetails: Return to full functional activity, pain-free prolonged walking and standing

patientAdvice.adviceDetails: Focus on restoring knee extension and improving single leg stability. Perform quadriceps and functional lower limb strengthening, improve ankle mobility, and activate posterior chain musculature. Rest during prolonged standing or walking when pain arises.
